summary: Remote shell over Cloudflare tunnel exposes installer host to full RCE
details: 9remote spawns a local PTY (bash/zsh/cmd/powershell via node-pty) and exposes it through a socket.io server tunneled over a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel. The socket.io `input` handler in dist/server.cjs writes remote-supplied bytes directly into the spawned PTY (`r.on("input", ({sessionId, data}) =>... i.pty.write(...))`), giving any party that completes the QR/apiKey pairing flow arbitrary command execution on the host running the tool. The Cloudflare tunnel makes the socket reachable from the public internet rather than restricted to LAN. The tool's `bin` is user-invoked (not install/import-time), and a `postinstall` step additionally provisions `~/.9remote/runtime` and installs the pinned `systray2@2.1.4` from the npm registry into that private path. The remote-shell surface is the package's advertised purpose, but network-sourced bytes reaching a local shell constitute a backdoor mechanism regardless of framing: pairing-flow weaknesses, key leakage, or a compromised rendezvous collapse to full-host RCE.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
